name: Mantario Trail
quote: Spanning an incredible 65 km through the Mantario Wilderness Zone in Whiteshell Provincial Park, the Mantario is Manitoba’s ultimate wilderness experience!
why: Multi-day backpacking trail through the Mantario Wilderness Zone; page gives 65 km (linear in practice, but page only says 'spanning').

name: Pine Point Self-guiding Trail
quote: Pine Point Self-guiding Trail, Whiteshell Provincial Park is a 5 km return trail to the scenic Pine Point Rapids.
why: Out-and-back trail to Pine Point Rapids; 5 km is the return distance.

name: McGillivray Falls Self-guiding Trail
quote: You may choose to hike the short loop of 2.8 km, or the longer 4.6-km trail which reaches McGillivray Lake.
why: Self-guiding trail past McGillivray Falls; the short loop is used (a longer 4.6 km option reaches McGillivray Lake).

name: Whiteshell River Self-guiding Trail
quote: The trail is 2.8 km long, with a few steep climbs up and down. Allow two hours to hike the trail.
why: Self-guiding trail; brochure gives 2.8 km but not whether loop or one way. Name is from the brochure title.

name: Amisk Trail
quote: The trail loops 4.3 kilometres through boreal forest, along the Rennie River
why: Self-guiding loop from the north end of Brereton Lake to the Rennie River below Inverness Falls (park info PDF gives 4.8 km).

name: Inverness Falls Trail
why: Short trail to Inverness Falls on the Rennie River, shown in the Amisk Trail brochure legend.

name: Bear Lake
quote: accessible from PTH 44, 13 km east of Rennie. Return distance 6 km. Allow two hours.
why: Rock-ridge and jack pine trail to Bear Lake off PTH 44 east of Rennie.

name: Big Whiteshell
quote: Return distance 1.5 km. Allow one hour.
why: Short viewpoint trail at the Big Whiteshell Lake recreation area.

name: Cabin Lake
quote: Accessible from Block 3, Red Rock subdivision road, west of PR 307. Return distance 4.6 km. Allow two hours.
why: Trail past a beaver dam to Cabin Lake from the Red Rock subdivision road.

name: Hunt Lake
quote: This 12.6-km (return) trail leads north to Indian Bay returning along the east shore of West Hawk Lake.
why: Steep trail from Hunt Lake on PTH 44 north along West Hawk Lake to Little Indian Bay.

name: Jessica Lake to Rainbow Falls
quote: Jessica Lake to Rainbow Falls, 8 km; allow three and a half hours.
why: Shield-country trail from the Jessica Lake Lodge staging area off PR 307 to Rainbow Falls (all distances stated as return).

name: Jessica Lake Loop A
why: Short loop at the Jessica Lake trail staging area off PR 307.

name: Jessica Lake Loop B
quote: In winter, Loop B is groomed for walking; 1.5 km; allow 45 min.
why: Short year-round walking loop at the Jessica Lake trail staging area.

name: Jessica Lake Loop C
quote: Loop C, 3.5 km; allow one and a half hours. All distances are return.
why: Longer loop at the Jessica Lake trail staging area off PR 307.

name: Alf Hole Goose Sanctuary
quote: A 2.5-km (return) trail has been developed in the sanctuary with signs explaining wildlife management techniques. Allow one hour.
why: Self-guiding trail in the Alfred Hole Goose Sanctuary near Rennie.

name: Falcon Creek
quote: Return distance 2.2 km. Allow one and a half hours.
why: Self-guiding geology trail north of the Trans-Canada Highway at the Falcon Lake entrance.

name: Forester's Footsteps
quote: Located at Betula Lake, this 2.4-km loop trail leads through jack pine and red pine plantations
why: Self-guiding forestry loop at Betula Lake on PR 307.

name: McGillivray Falls long loop
quote: Long loop is 4.6 km; allow three hours.
why: Longer of the two McGillivray Falls loops off PTH 44 near Caddy Lake (the 2.8 km short loop is already proposed).

name: Meditation Lake
quote: A 1.5 km walk in to Meditation Lake is another easy overnight backcountry experience.
why: Short walk-in trail to backcountry campsites on Meditation Lake.
